extracted.intended_audience: writers, translators, and the literary community (potential applicants, nominees, and readers of PEN America awards)
extracted.subtask_description: Overview of the PEN America Literary Awards program: the organization's goals, the kinds of works and genres it recognizes, and the award processes (longlists, finalists, winners, and special honors).

rubrics_metrics.name: Outstanding voices in literature
rubrics_metrics.description: Since 1963, the PEN America Literary Awards have honored many of the most outstanding voices in literature across diverse genres.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: This is a high-level selection standard: the awards seek to recognize writers viewed as 'outstanding' within their field; the page lists the range of genres considered (see 'Genre diversity' entry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Original and promising writers
rubrics_metrics.description: “The PEN America Literary Awards work to elevate original and promising voices and build a literary canon fit for the 21st century.” / “we seek to champion original and promising writers of the global community”
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Emphasis on originality and 'promise' indicates judges prioritize innovation and potential as selection qualities across many awards.

rubrics_metrics.name: Genre and form diversity
rubrics_metrics.description: Awards honor work 'across diverse genres, including fiction, poetry, science writing, essays, sports writing, biography, children’s literature, and drama.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Explicitly accepts and evaluates work across multiple literary genres and forms; eligibility/recognition is organized by genre-specific categories.

rubrics_metrics.name: Multiple award types and monetary support
rubrics_metrics.description: PEN America, with the help of our partners, confers over 20 distinct awards, fellowships, grants and prizes each year, awarding nearly $350,000 to writers and translators.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Programmatic criterion: different awards have different formats (awards vs. fellowships/grants/prizes) and monetary amounts; applicants should attend to the specific award type and its requirements.

rubrics_metrics.name: Honorary and career-achievement recognition
rubrics_metrics.description: Tom Stoppard, M. NourbeSe Philip, Tanya Barfield, Rigoberto González to Receive PEN America Honorary and Career-Achievement Literary Awards
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Some PEN awards recognize lifetime or career achievement and function differently from single-work prizes; nomination/selection for these honors focuses on sustained contribution rather than a single submission.

rubrics_metrics.name: Nomination awards and category-specific achievement
rubrics_metrics.description: 2019 PEN America honors achievement in international literature, editing, literary sports writing, and drama, and literary promise in poetry.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Certain awards are nomination-based and target particular achievements (editing, sports writing, international literature, etc.) or signals of promise within a genre (e.g., poetry).

rubrics_metrics.name: Selection process: longlists, finalists, and judges
rubrics_metrics.description: Announcements include 'longlists,' 'finalists,' and 'winners' and the site invites readers to 'Meet the ... Literary Awards Judges.'
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluation is multi-stage (longlist → finalists → winners) and conducted by panels of judges; applicants should expect a judged selection pipeline and publicized shortlists.

rubrics_metrics.name: Submission cycles and timelines
rubrics_metrics.description: Submissions for the 2020 Awards cycle are now closed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Awards operate on annual cycles with submission windows and deadlines; prospective entrants must track yearly submission periods and related announcements.
